title: Preflight Request
body:
Before certain cross-origin requests, the browser sends an automatic `OPTIONS` request asking the server, in effect, "if I sent this for real, would you allow it?" The server answers with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, and only if that answer permits it does the browser send the actual request.

Two things trip people up. First, **your JavaScript never writes this request** — the browser generates it on its own, which is why an `OPTIONS` you never coded shows up in the Network tab. Second, it's only triggered for non-"simple" requests: anything using PUT/PATCH/DELETE, a custom header, or a `Content-Type` like `application/json`. A plain GET or a form-style POST skips preflight, goes straight to the server, and gets blocked only afterwards at the response-reading step. See [[CORS]] and [[Same-Origin Policy]].
